description: Re-scoped CAM-5 (filed pre-CAM-42). The literal --max-turns / --max-budget-usd flags are print-mode-only, so they require claude -p which is forbidden for subscription accounts (CAM-42); USD budget is also N/A on a subscription (no per-call billing). The valid, unaddressed core is a per-worker cost ceiling: today the only per-worker bound is the wall-clock perWorkerTimeoutMs. Deliver the spirit via the available mechanism: the supervisor already reads a worker's cumulative token spend from its transcript (parseTranscriptUsage), and the transcript grows during the session, so the sentinel poll loop can read the spend each tick and kill the worker pane when it crosses an opt-in token ceiling. The 'turns' half of the original ask is already covered by the existing supervisor maxIterations cap (MAX_ITERATIONS=50, src/supervisor/loop.ts); only the cost half needs a new mechanism, delivered here as the token ceiling.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: --max-turns ('Limit the number of agentic turns (print mode only)') and --max-budget-usd ('Maximum dollar amount to spend on API calls before stopping (print mode only)') are BOTH documented as print-mode-only, i.e. they require -p/--print. Since claude -p is forbidden for subscription accounts (CAM-42), neither flag is usable in the interactive TUI worker model. The per-worker ceiling must therefore be enforced supervisor-side, by polling the worker transcript token usage, not via a claude flag.

userStories.title: Enforce an opt-in per-worker token ceiling in the sentinel poll loop
userStories.description: As the supervisor, I want to kill a worker that exceeds a configured cumulative token ceiling, so a runaway interactive worker has a cost guardrail beyond the wall-clock timeout (the --max-turns/--max-budget-usd flags are print-mode-only and unusable under the subscription rule).
acceptanceCriteria: src/supervisor/loop.ts gains a maxWorkerTokens option (number; default 0 meaning DISABLED / no ceiling).

TokensEventDetail (src/supervisor/events.ts) and the readWorkerTokens mapping are extended to include cacheCreationTokens (parseTranscriptUsage already computes usage.cacheCreation; the current mapping drops it). This is required so the poll-loop ceiling can use the same spend definition as the orchestrator budget.

When maxWorkerTokens > 0 AND readWorkerTokens is available, the sentinel poll loop reads the worker's cumulative token spend each tick (after the pane-alive and sentinel checks), computed as input + cacheCreation + cacheRead (the SAME formula as computeOrchBudget in src/orchestrator/budget.ts, now that cacheCreation is carried on the detail).

When the spend >= maxWorkerTokens, the supervisor kills the worker pane (respawn-pane -k with a harmless echo, like the timeout branch), emits a 'worker-token-ceiling' event with detail { spend, ceiling }, calls notifyTerminal('blocked'), and returns { status: 'blocked', ... }. This is a terminal stop (re-dispatching would only burn more tokens): it does NOT go through the dead-worker backoff/retry path.
When maxWorkerTokens is 0 / unset, behavior is unchanged: no token polling, no kill (the existing pane-alive / sentinel / timeout logic is untouched).
'worker-token-ceiling' is added to the WorkerEventKind union in src/supervisor/events.ts (closed union).

Adding cacheCreationTokens to TokensEventDetail does not break existing consumers/tests of the 'tokens' event (it is an additive field; update any exact-shape assertion in test/supervisor/ if present).

Tests: with an injected readWorkerTokens returning escalating spend and maxWorkerTokens set, the worker is killed and the loop returns 'blocked' with a 'worker-token-ceiling' event once the ceiling is crossed; with maxWorkerTokens 0, readWorkerTokens is never consulted in the poll and no kill happens.
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/loop.ts (sentinel poll loop ~lines 545-553; readWorkerTokens injected ~line 402), src/supervisor/events.ts (TokensEventDetail ~85 + readWorkerTokens mapping ~213 + WorkerEventKind union ~51), test/supervisor/loop.test.ts (+ test/supervisor/events.test.ts if it asserts the tokens detail shape). computeOrchBudget (src/orchestrator/budget.ts) spend = input + cacheCreation + cacheRead is the canonical definition to mirror; the worker ceiling must match it, which is WHY TokensEventDetail must carry cacheCreation (it currently drops it). parseTranscriptUsage already returns usage.cacheCreation. Default 0 = disabled is deliberate (opt-in hard brake; rate-limit is the natural backstop). The transcript grows during the session so polling readWorkerTokens(uuid) gives cumulative-so-far.

userStories.title: Wire the CAM_WORKER_MAX_TOKENS knob and document the per-worker guardrails
userStories.description: As an operator, I want to opt into the per-worker token ceiling via an env var, and I want the docs to record which guardrails exist and why the claude -p flags are not used.
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/next.ts parses CAM_WORKER_MAX_TOKENS (positive integer; default 0 = disabled) exactly the way CAM_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS is parsed, and passes it as maxWorkerTokens to runSupervisor.

A test (test/next.test.ts or equivalent) injects a stubbed supervisorFn and asserts that runNext forwards the parsed maxWorkerTokens AND the readWorkerTokens adapter into the runSupervisor options (a non-trivial behavioral gate, not just a precondition).

FLOW.md and/or docs/recovery-runbook.md document the per-worker guardrails: the wall-clock perWorkerTimeoutMs (CAM_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS) and the opt-in token ceiling (CAM_WORKER_MAX_TOKENS), and note that --max-turns / --max-budget-usd are print-mode-only (ruled out by the claude -p ban, CAM-42), that USD budget is N/A on a subscription, and that the 'turns' cap is the existing maxIterations.
The recovery-runbook event-log section lists the 'worker-token-ceiling' event (grep returns it).
No em-dash in the edited markdown (use colon, comma, parens, or period).
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/next.ts (CAM_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS parsing is at ~lines 297-305; mirror it for CAM_WORKER_MAX_TOKENS, default 0; pass maxWorkerTokens into the runSupervisor options object ~line 714). Docs: FLOW.md (the cam next / supervisor section) and docs/recovery-runbook.md (event-log diagnostics section + a per-worker-guardrails note).
